name: entropy-coded-bf16-hostile-codec
the_result: HELD. An entropy-coded, sequential, instance-sized representation (`BF16_ZLIB`) executes through registration alone: one `.register` line, zero edits to prepared.rs, production.rs, physical.rs, weights/mod.rs or operands.rs, and the candidate container's logits are bit-exact to the raw-bf16 control's under the production backend. The one contract leak the forecast named — shape-derived storage size — was the one that surfaced, and it cost exactly one refusal variant in the contract's vocabulary; every other contract file is byte-identical to f92fac65. The row-random consumer refuses the codec by access class before reading a byte.

the_claim_this_earns.before: LARQL has a representation registry and an extensible codec/execution contract — registry-pluggable representation IMPLEMENTATIONS, not runtime-pluggable packages.
the_claim_this_earns.now: LARQL supports plug-in representations with different storage and access semantics. Evidence: a representation that violates the mmap / random-access assumptions of every prior codec was made executable by registering it, with the executor untouched.
the_claim_this_earns.not_yet: 'representation-open' waits on VQ (represented auxiliary dependencies) and progressive (selectable extents). Pluggable LOWERING TARGETS — a second and third registry for execution providers and artifact projections — are enabled by this seam but not delivered; rung 3's planner-visible admission and realization trace is their prerequisite.

findings_not_in_the_forecast.finding: The reader-adapter inflater conflates 'input ended' with 'stream ended'. A stream missing its final Adler-32 byte decoded WHOLE and was accepted: the DEFLATE data was complete, the adapter returned end-of-file at the missing trailer, and nothing distinguished that from a verified end. The generalized ranges.rs:87 gate — the arm that says an instance-sized codec must refuse a short stream at decode — is what caught it.
findings_not_in_the_forecast.fix: decode_rows inflates through the low-level `Decompress` API and, for a whole decode, requires `Status::StreamEnd` (the trailer read and verified), refuses an image longer than the shape through a one-byte spare buffer, refuses a stream that ends before its trailer, and refuses bytes after the stream. A prefix decode judges only that the prefix exists — as preregistered.
findings_not_in_the_forecast.lesson: The trailer must be positively witnessed; 'no more input' is not 'the stream vouched for itself'. And the gate that found it was a universal quantifier I had just weakened — weakening it by DECLARATION rather than by label is why it still had teeth.

findings_not_in_the_forecast.finding: The forecast's W3 wording 'index.json byte-identical between the two containers' was impossible: index.json records payload_bytes / payload_sha256 / segment_sha256 per representation entry (index.rs:32-38), so two containers with different payload bytes cannot share an index. A reconnaissance miss.
findings_not_in_the_forecast.resolution: The witness re-records the rewritten segments in the index exactly as the compiler does (compile/mod.rs:180), asserts the two indexes equal modulo those three fields of the transcoded entries, verifies the recorded segment hashes against the files, and compares every other regular file byte for byte with equal name sets asserted first.

findings_not_in_the_forecast.finding: Packed MXFP4 expert banks are labelled `U8` in the tensor table (experts.rs DTYPE_U8) — a label outside the registry, judged by the bank loader's own arm. The new preflight therefore applies only to registered labels and leaves the U8 dialect on its existing path unchanged.
findings_not_in_the_forecast.for_rung_3: The row-random consumer's dtype vocabulary is not fully registry-backed; the same is true of the seam's `stored_bf16` / `stored_nvfp4` booleans (prepared.rs:685-697). Planner-visible admission has to replace both with codec declarations.

findings_not_in_the_forecast.finding: W4 lives at `coverage_experts_production/bf16_zlib_bank.rs`, not in `bf16_zlib_execution.rs` as forecast: the routed fixture's builders are `pub(super)` inside that module and a witness that reuses them has to be its descendant. Widening the fixture's visibility would have been the alternative; moving the test was the smaller change. `coverage_experts_production.rs` gains one `mod` line.

The only BF16_ZLIB encoder lives in `format/vindex3/fixtures.rs` (`encode_bf16_zlib`), the crate's public fixture module, so both the codec tests and the execution witnesses reach it. The compile path (`arena.rs` encode table, `compile.rs` bank pricing) is untouched and cannot emit BF16_ZLIB — as forecast: encode is not part of the contract.
The container written by `encode_system` holds a subdirectory as well as files; the first byte-comparison read it as a file. The comparison is over regular files.

contract_verdict.trait_surfaces: unchanged — every signature and provided method of RepresentationCodec, every capability / residency / extent / stream / geometry type, byte-identical to f92fac65
contract_verdict.contract_vocabulary: +1 refusal: CodecError::InstanceSized. Reported as a contract change because the user asked for that honesty; the freeze decides whether vocabulary growth counts
observations_for_the_freeze: ExtentCertificate.bits_per_weight has no vocabulary for a variable-rate code; BF16_ZLIB certifies the supremum (16.0) and its tests pin instances on both sides of it. Whether the freeze wants a rate/bound distinction is open.

ResidencyProfile prices resident image only; source traffic is undeclared for every realization of every codec. BF16_ZLIB makes the gap visible because its stored length is instance-dependent, falling on either side of the shape-derived image. The census witness reads source touch from the container's recorded length instead.
validate() for an instance-sized codec can judge only the header; 'length against shape' moves to decode. The trait allows this; the gates that assumed otherwise were tests.
